direct_answer.precise_boundary: Use the California Housing task objective and declared split/metric as source material only. Do not use AgentHPOBench's fixed-menu, repeated-test, archive-best protocol as the P0. A separate task-bound apparatus must create open code-level research, dev-only feedback, one agent-selected frozen prediction artifact, and immutable external hidden scoring without changing the dataset target, split algorithm, units, or raw RMSE.
direct_answer.why_not_admitted: License/data/dependency receipts, custody, artifact contract, scorer independence, deterministic replay, measured compute, invalid/missing/retry rules, MUE and exact user execution approval remain open.

source_facts.fact: The pinned AgentHPOBench source is OpenMOSS/AgentHPOBench commit 6d8d90071cdb16b06f0db866480ecaae48880fba, tree 1acedca0a63252deea57a51878b4ddfd002aa507; the parent-provided manifest records 798 verified files.
The benchmark is explicitly one baseline plus five sequential interventions over constrained configuration spaces.
For the generic tasks, the strict runner repeats the task evaluator five times, passes prior result histories to decisions, then chooses the best intervention by the reported metric.

The result-integrity layer audits traces, fallbacks, errors, raw decision responses, seeds and model identifiers. Its "artifact" search is for agent response/error files, not a locked ML model or prediction artifact.
Task repositories, datasets and weights are excluded from this source tree, and the project says each upstream component remains under its own terms.

The three shortlisted evaluators train locally from source without a task-side model download/API call in the inspected code. Their released agent runners separately default to local Qwen weights and CUDA.
All three task preparation scripts require pre-staged files; none provides a source URL plus cryptographic dataset hash and license receipt.
All three shortlisted task loops expose test metrics to the decision process; none emits a scoreable frozen prediction/model artifact.

Several attractive-looking small tasks were not shortlisted because their own metadata identifies a generated deterministic bandit, a heuristic 2048 policy, or a 120-step vanilla-backend parity substitute.

common_blockers.detail: All candidate decisions are clamped to enumerated configuration menus. Wide/narrow variants only transform those menus. There is no code-level hypothesis/experiment/decision record surface.
The agent sees test metrics after each run, and the strict wrapper chooses the best test-scored intervention. This is neither hidden scoring nor single agent selection.
Evaluators write metrics JSON. Integrity code checks decision-response files, not model/prediction bytes.
Training, test evaluation, metric emission and runner selection are coupled in the same task code/process boundary.
Only the benchmark Apache license is in the audited tree. Upstream/data terms, data hashes and exact task environments are external or absent.
Epoch counts and device defaults are source declarations, not measurements; no clean replay or resource receipt was produced.

required_task_bound_closures_before_any_: Acquire candidate source/data under a reviewed license chain; record URLs, revisions, byte hashes, terms, and ancestry.
Freeze one reproducible environment and command. Measure clean-install success, wall time, RAM/VRAM, and score replay tolerance on the available compute.
Freeze train/dev/hidden membership and custody. The agent must not receive hidden labels, the full reconstructible source table, or a bypass path.
Use public/dev outcomes only for research decisions. Keep hidden score unavailable until after exactly one eligible artifact is locked.
Define the sole artifact schema, ID/order/finite-value validation, hash+timestamp lock, no-lock/fallback rule, mutation rejection and one scorer call.
Keep scorer code/data outside the editable arm workspace. Score only artifact bytes; ignore any agent-authored results.json.
Replace the fixed menu with an arm-common editable solution layer, while freezing dataset, split algorithm, metric, budget and allowed dependencies.
Preregister raw task metric as primary; do not use archive-best or the paper-anchor normalized score as primary.
Close invalid/missing/retry/repair/no-replacement, MUE, latency/gate/R2 census and P0 development-ancestry requirements from the current contract.
Obtain independent task-bound protocol review and exact user execution approval. Apparatus authorization is not P0 execution authority.

findings: Repeated access to the same test metric permits adaptive test tuning.
Archive-best selection makes primary outcome a mechanical oracle choice, not the agent-selected locked artifact.
Known paper anchors and the TabM winning-like recipe are included in prompts.
An editable research arm could simply alter results.json unless scorer input is limited to immutable prediction bytes.
Normalized improvement against mismatched full-paper anchors can magnify small noisy differences; use raw task metric for P0.

evidence.claim: Pinned source identity and verified-file count are manifest facts.
Only apparatus/static mocks are approved; native changes and a specific scientific run are not authorized.
The task-bound contract requires a single agent-selected frozen artifact before hidden scoring and forbids archive-best replacement.
AgentHPOBench declares one baseline plus five interventions and a constrained intervention space.
Upstream source, data, weights and credentials are outside this repository; task-specific licenses remain external.
The strict runner performs five prior-result-dependent decisions but selects the best intervention by the reported task metric, not an agent-locked final artifact.
The strict runner loads task modules into its own process and consumes task result dictionaries.

Published integrity checks validate trace, fallback, errors, raw agent-response artifacts, seed and model provenance; they do not validate a frozen ML prediction/model artifact or independent hidden scorer.
Search-space variants remain menu transformations rather than open code or method proposals.
Dependency provenance is not task-lock complete.
TabM declares a 64/16/20 seed-1 split, 50 epochs, validation selection and a fixed finite model/config menu.
TabM dataset preparation only checks pre-staged files and shape; it supplies no download URL, checksum or data-license receipt.
TabM adapter uses a local PlainMLP or external tabm implementation; it reads all labels, selects on validation, evaluates test, supports a source-level CPU fallback, and writes only results.json.
TabM agent context exposes test RMSE and an official winning-like recipe before selection.
SparseTSF declares public ETTm1 provenance, horizon-96, one epoch and a finite menu.

SparseTSF preparation only checks pre-staged data and upstream source; the evaluator imports the official model and implements explicit chronological train/validation/test boundaries with train-fitted scaling.
SparseTSF evaluates test every epoch and writes metrics JSON without a model or prediction artifact.
SparseTSF agent context exposes test MSE from prior trials and accepts only one NEW_CONFIG from the finite space.
VBLL declares a seed-1 72/18/10 split, 80 epochs and a finite configuration menu.
VBLL preparation only checks a pre-staged UCI file; its model uses the external vbll Regression layer.
VBLL evaluator reads and splits all labels, evaluates test, and writes only results.json.
VBLL agent context exposes test RMSE/NLL from prior trials and accepts only one NEW_CONFIG from the menu.
Synthetic/heuristic shortlist exclusions are explicitly labeled in metadata.
Candidate upstream revisions are pinned, with TabM specifically only an audited source subset and VBLL/SparseTSF described as exact trees.
The released task runners default to a local Qwen3-32B decision model, while the strict wrapper defaults to Qwen3-8B and a CUDA device; these are runner requirements, not task-model necessities.
